The statement reduces every certificate to a directly computable sum of independent durations compared with T, eliminating any need to reason about scheduling order.
The promise that exactly one certificate is applicable, allowing a first-match JOB check followed by fixed-priority load checks.
The statement directly characterizes infeasibility as either one pair sum p1+p2 exceeding T or one track's total segment length exceeding T, and promises that one such certificate exists.
The geometry is a one-dimensional interval-packing problem whose feasibility is completely characterized by additive lengths: p1+p2 for one motif and the channel-wide sums for alpha or beta.
The statement makes every feasibility question cardinality-only: injectivity and pairwise disjointness turn the function requirements into local p1+p2 and global sum-of-p1/sum-of-p2 pigeonhole tests.

per_depth.common_affordance: The explicit guarantee that exactly one independent requirement is broken, making direct scalar feasibility tests and fixed precedence sufficient.
The firewall plus independent one-packet-per-channel capacities make feasibility completely characterizable by three scalar inequalities: p1_i + p2_i > T, sum(p1_i) > T, or sum(p2_i) > T.
The specified Snapshot-before-Delta ordering makes every Snapshot counted toward the final tracker need a distinct second after all Delta chunks, yielding the shortcut p1 + p2 > T.
